title: Pas de Deux

beats.what: Boyd tries to apologise to Donna for hiding Sara; she stays silent and leaves
Donna reports the food supply to Colony House; only a month of rations remain
Kristi discovers Marielle stole morphine from the clinic supply; confrontation in the infirmary
Boyd confesses to Kenny that worms are crawling under his skin and asks Kenny to kill him if it gets bad
Food-shortage panic erupts; Dale stabs Ellis with a knife during the confrontation
Boyd reveals his worm infection to Kristi, who catches him talking to an invisible figure in the basement
Boyd draws the infection out of himself and lures the worms into his own body to spare Ellis a tainted transfusion
Boyd donates blood directly after purging the worms; Ellis stabilises
Fatima privately asks Kristi for a pregnancy test, ending the episode

character_beats.beat: Wants to protect everyone; forces himself to stay useful as leader while internally terrified the infection will consume him
Wants to trust Boyd; is pushed into performing emergency surgery on Ellis while Boyd withholds the full truth of what is in his blood
Claims she had the addiction under control; her relapse forces Kristi's hand and almost loses Ellis the medical care he needs

key_lines.line: You'll put an end to things before it goes too far.
key_lines.why: Boyd frames his own death as a mercy request, inverting his usual protector role

key_lines.line: I don't wanna die like Martin died.
key_lines.why: Names the worst possible fate and makes it concrete; the worm infection is not abstract

key_lines.line: I got worms under my skin.
key_lines.why: First on-screen admission of the infection's progression to a third party

key_lines.line: My blood is your blood now, motherfucker.
key_lines.why: Boyd inverts the cave man's ritual phrase, weaponising the infection against the worm entity

key_lines.line: Sometimes crazy is the most rational response you could have.
key_lines.why: The imagined Khatri grants Boyd permission to act outside normal logic

open_loops: What exactly are the worms Boyd expelled and where did they go after leaving his body?
Did any trace of the infection transfer to Ellis through the transfusion despite Boyd's attempt to purge it first?
Fatima's impossible pregnancy: what does it mean in a place that kills people?
Will Kristi report Boyd's breakdown and confession to the rest of the community?

payoffs.plants_from: S02E05 (previous: blood ritual scene with cave man)
payoffs.what: Boyd's worm infection, introduced when the cave man cut his arm, now has visible physical symptoms and a ticking clock

payoffs.plants_from: S02E05 (Marielle on bus heading to rehab)
payoffs.what: Marielle's concealed relapse explodes into the open, directly triggering the food-pantry confrontation

contradiction.wants: to be honest with his community and lean on others for help
contradiction.does: withholds the full danger of his infection from Kristi even as he begs for her assistance, risking Ellis's life by not telling her what is in his blood

tone_notes: Dense first act (132 w/min) drops sharply to near-silence between 05:58 and 07:39 (101-second top silence) marking the gap between Boyd's apology scene and the food-supply crisis. A second hard silence at 41:13-42:05 (52 sec) falls exactly after the transfusion line is placed, letting the weight of what Boyd just did breathe. Minutes 32-34 spike to 206-244 w/min, the highest density of the episode, coinciding with the Dale stabbing and the race to the clinic.
